newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - June 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - June 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- WEN WEI PO -- The Hong Kong garrison of the People's Liberation Army will open some of its bases to the public at "an appropriate time" to enhance understanding between Hong Kong people and the Chinese soldiers.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Speaking on the annual meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said that Hong Kong's return to the mainland would enhance prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region. He stressed that China would strengthen its relationship with Asia and the world.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Hong Kong's graft watchdog, the Independent Commission Against Corruption, has decided to use more professional methods to train undercover officers and take a more aggressive approach when investigating cases. The decision came amid public concern that corruption would worsen after the handover.
-- MING PAO -- Two New York-based fund management companies were warned by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority for helping clients speculate against the Hong Kong dollar on July 18.

-- SING TAO -- A recent survey showed that money, material comfort and social status are what most Beijing young people are after. The two most popular choices of profession among teenagers in Chinese capital are businessman and showbiz star.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Hated Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot was seen and photographed for the first time in 18 years by American journalist Nate Thayer. The shadowy war criminal, recently reported dead, was apparently seen on trial in Cambodia's northern jungles last week.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Secretary for Justice Elsie Leung said the government had a contingency plan in case the Court of Appeal ruled on Tuesday that the Provisional Legislature, which replaced the elected Legislative Council on July 1, was illegal.
